description: We are SATelligence, a multidisciplinary team from Haifa, Israel, combining expertise in Earth Observation, remote sensing, data science, AI, environmental engineering, and entrepreneurship. We bring together academic research, industry experience, and technological innovation to address real-world environmental challenges. Our goal is to transform complex scientific data into practical and scalable data.
summary:
Coffee is a globally vital crop supporting millions of livelihoods, yet climate change threatens its future through rising temperatures, unpredictable rainfall and soil degradation.

Coffee Shift by SATelligence is a user-friendly decision-support application that transforms NASA Earth observation data into actionable insights for non-technical farmers. By integrating satellite-derived environmental indicators, local soil conditions, and farmer preferences, it assesses coffee-field conditions and provides personalized crop-rotation, intercropping and climate-adaptation recommendations with practical implementation timelines.

Our innovation goes beyond monitoring: we bridge the gap between complex satellite data and real-world agricultural decisions, empowering farmers to make informed, climate-resilient choices. Starting with coffee and designed to scale to other crops and regions, Coffee Shift supports UN SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) and SDG 13 (Climate Action) by promoting sustainable, climate-smart agriculture.
details:
Coffee Shift is a farmer-centered decision-support application developed to help coffee growers understand their field conditions and adapt to climate change. It bridges the gap between complex Earth observation data and practical agricultural decisions, making environmental information accessible to non-technical users.

How it work: The application combines NASA Earth observation data with local soil characteristics and farmer preferences to assess coffee-growing conditions. Our analysis incorporates precipitation from NASA GPM/IMERG, tree canopy cover from MODIS, elevation and slope from SRTM,and soil pH estimates from ISRIC SoilGrids and more.

These indicators provide insights into water availability, potential shading, terrain characteristics and soil suitability. The application is designed to translate these insights into personalized recommendations for intercropping, crop rotation where applicable and climate-adaptation practices, supported by actionable timelines.

Tools and technologies: We used NASA data stored by Google Earth Engine (GEE) and more NASA references tools (listed in references) to process and analyze geospatial datasets, extract environmental indicators for a selected coffee field in Brazil as a pilot area and export results for further analysis.

Innovation and impact: Rather than simply visualizing satellite data, Coffee Shift aims to connect environmental monitoring with practical, farm-specific recommendations. Its farmer-centered approach considers local environmental conditions, crop requirements and individual farmer priorities. Beyond environmental resilience, Coffee Shift introduces economic value by helping farmers anticipate production capacity, assess their ability to meet supply commitments and make informed decisions that strengthen supply-chain reliability, protect livelihoods and support the wider agricultural economy.The goal is to support informed agricultural decisions, improve climate resilience and make satellite-based insights accessible to farmers without specialized technical knowledge.

Starting with coffee, our approach is designed to be adaptable to other crops and geographic regions, contributing to UN SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).
